claims.statement: Every data-channel message is a protobuf Message (ts-proto-generated from src/proto/message.proto) carrying a file id plus exactly one payload: metaData, chunk, or receiveEvent (ACCEPT/REJECT/RECEIVED_CHUNK/VALIDATE_ERROR).
File ids are crypto.randomUUID() values rather than filenames, so same-named files in one session keep distinct ids and their chunks never cross-wire; metaData.name is used for display only.

The sender maintains per-file state in a reactive map with lifecycle Pending -> WaitingAccept -> Processing -> Success; on ACCEPT it starts the chunk loop, on REJECT or VALIDATE_ERROR it records the error and resets the file to Pending (retryable); the async event handlers re-read the live entry after each await and bail if it was removed, and chunk-send failures land as visible error entries instead of unhandled rejections (via the shared markChunkFailed helper, deduplicated in PR #70); a connectionLost flag set by onChannelClose marks the channel as dead so in-flight pipelines exit quietly with accurate connection-lost errors instead of per-chunk InvalidStateError failures (PR #74), and the SendingFileList UI hides the Resend/Continue/Send buttons (leaving only Remove) when the channel is lost because each would be a guaranteed silent no-op.

The transfer protocol is receiver-ack chunking: the receiver enqueues each incoming chunk onto a per-file serialized chain (onChunkData), and processChunk sends EVENT_RECEIVED_CHUNK after successful decryption and a re-check that the file is still active, so the sender sends at most one next chunk per ack until offset reaches metaData.size — backpressure pacing the transfer with the sender one round-trip ahead.

A defensive empty-chunk guard aborts the send with an 'Invalid chunk size' error when a chunk reads 0 bytes while bytes remain, preventing an infinite loop of empty sends caused by an invalid chunkSize (e.g. a crafted 'c' URL param).

Progress and bitrate UI updates are throttled by PROGRESS_UPDATE_UI_STEP (3 percentage points) using non-reactive stats mirrors, and pause/resume is implemented via a per-file stop flag where onContinue re-emits a synthetic RECEIVED_CHUNK event to restart the chunk loop — except on a dead channel (connectionLost), where onContinue no-ops so a resume cannot emit a synthetic ack into a pipeline whose next send would just no-op.

The receiver keeps per-file chunk buffers, byte counters, and per-file processing chains in deliberately non-reactive plain objects (receivingFileChunkMap / receivingFileStatsMap / chunkQueue) so chunk arrival does not trigger Svelte re-renders; only the reactive receivingFiles map is flushed at the 3-point progress step.

On completion (receivedSize exactly equals the declared size) the receiver builds the file Blob immediately, deletes both per-file state maps, and releases the file's chunkQueue entry — releasing the raw per-chunk buffers so a large file is not held twice in memory.

validateFileMetadata is the single size gate and enforces two bounds because metaData.size is peer-controlled: a size that is not finite or is <= 0 is rejected with 'invalid file size' (such a value would otherwise make the receiver flip the file to Success on a partial/empty payload or break the progress math), and size > maxSize (default 1 GB via DEFAULT_RECEIVE_OPTIONS) fails with a limit message; receiver-side validation failure sends EVENT_VALIDATE_ERROR back to the sender and records the error on the file, while autoAccept (default true) makes the receiver accept valid files without user action.

The data channel is created ordered:false, so chunk ordering is enforced by the protocol (one receiver ack drives one sender chunk, isolated per file id) rather than by channel-level ordering; completion is exact-declared-size based with no trailer or checksum.

onMetaData registers the file entry at WaitingAccept BEFORE the async AES key decryption, so the file is visible and removable throughout; if the RSA key unwrap fails, the entry gets a visible error, an error toast fires, and EVENT_VALIDATE_ERROR is sent to the sender (bouncing its file to Pending) instead of the file silently never appearing while the sender waits for an accept that will not come; the metadata-failed entry stays in WaitingAccept with the error shown, so it is not a Remove-only dead-end (PR #76) — but an Accept on it is refused by the onAccept guard (PR #78): explanatory toast plus EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT, no state change, no chunk map, leaving Deny/Remove as the real exits.

Per-file chunk processing is serialized on a per-file promise chain (serializeTask): processChunk for chunk N+1 cannot start before chunk N's processing has settled, so decrypt/push/stats/blob-on-complete run in strict arrival order even when WebCrypto decrypt completions are out of order; the chain's catch routes any error to rejectCorruptChunk (idempotent — no-op once the per-file chunk map is gone) instead of swallowing it, so a failed chunk can never leave the file permanently incomplete or stall the queue.

Late or stray chunks are dropped, not fatal: onChunkData ignores chunks for unknown or uninitialized file ids (metadata never registered, file removed/denied, or already completed), and processChunk re-checks the chunk map after the decrypt await so a file removed/denied mid-flight is dropped without acking (an ack would advance the sender past a rejected file).

Bulk download builds a real store-only ZIP archive in memory (createZipStoreOnly: method-0 entries, CRC-32, UTF-8 name flag, duplicate-name disambiguation that checks each candidate against every already-emitted final name so pre-suffixed peer-controlled names cannot collide, no new dependency) and saves a single zero-share-files.zip via triggerDownload, instead of the former sequential per-file raw downloads that never produced a zip; onDownload null-guards the entry so a missing/duplicated key no longer throws an unhandled TypeError and skips the per-file teardown.

All receiver downloads route through triggerDownload, which defers URL.revokeObjectURL ~1 second after clicking the temporary download anchor, because revoking in the same tick can abort the async download in some engines (e.g. Firefox starting the fetch after the revoke).

MetaData.size is int64 on the wire (PR #42 / commit 721c502; was int32), so files of 2 GiB or larger no longer throw 'invalid int32' during Message.encode; tests/protocol-size.test.mjs pins this by encoding and round-tripping 3 GiB and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER sizes through the generated proto code.

The receiver 'Max Size' dropdown options carry true byte values matching their labels (10 MB = 10 * 1024 * 1024, 100 MB = 100 * 1024 * 1024, 'Unlimit' = 1 TiB); previously the 10/100 MB options were 1024x smaller than their labels and enforced KB limits (PR #44). onChange coerces the select value with Number(maxSize) and falls back to DEFAULT_RECEIVE_OPTIONS.maxSize when not finite, because bind:value on a <select> yields a string after user interaction, so ReceiveOptions.maxSize stays a number at runtime. tests/receiver-options-size.test.mjs statically pins these option values and the coercion.

Chunk size is enforced numeric on two layers: Sender.sendNextChunk defensively coerces its chunkSize prop with Number() (32 KB fallback for non-finite/non-positive values) so a string from a <select> bind:value can no longer make offset + chunkSize concatenate and send the whole file remainder as one over-sized chunk, and OfferOptions.onChange coerces the select value with Number() and falls back to DEFAULT_SEND_OPTIONS.chunkSize when it is not in CHUNK_SIZE_OPTIONS, keeping sendOptions.chunkSize a number at the source.

A chunk that fails AES-GCM authentication is rejected visibly, not dropped: processChunk routes the decrypt failure to rejectCorruptChunk, which marks the file errored ('corrupt data in transit'), bounces the status back to Pending, toasts the failure, sends EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT so the sender stops cleanly, and tears down the per-file chunk/stats/queue state — instead of the byte count never catching up and the file sitting in Processing forever; the EVENT_RECEIVED_CHUNK ack is sent only after successful decryption so a corrupt chunk never advances the sender.

The sender's document-level paste listener is scoped to file sharing: handlePasteEvent ignores events whose target is an INPUT, TEXTAREA, SELECT, or content-editable element, so pasting an answer code or custom ICE server value into any text field no longer silently adds a stray clipboard.txt to the sender file list, and onDestroy removes the listener so it never outlives the component.

Removing a file while its chunk pipeline is in flight is safe: onRemove sets the stop flag (when Processing) before deleting the entry; the async pipeline only ever dereferences the entry reference captured at onSend entry (never a live re-read of sendingFiles[key] after an await), re-checks stop and the live entry at every await boundary, and the event handlers bail when the live entry is gone — so no continuation can dereference a deleted entry (previously an uncaught TypeError from sendingFiles[key].aesKey/.progress) or send a chunk into the void; onContinue likewise refuses to re-enter the pipeline on a dead channel (connectionLost).

Because metaData.size is peer-controlled and is the receiver's completion gate, the receiver validates it with a lower bound: validateFileMetadata rejects a size that is not finite or is <= 0 with an explicit 'invalid file size' error (such a value would otherwise complete the file on the first chunk with a partial/empty payload, or make the progress math NaN/negative and break the progress UI), and the per-chunk progress ratio is clamped to [0, 100] before reaching the UI as defense in depth on top of the exact-match gate and the overshoot reject.

onAccept (the shared entry point of autoAccept and the list UI's Accept button) guards up front against metadata-failed entries — error set (key decryption or max-size validation), or an encrypted session with no aesKey (PR #78): it toasts 'Cannot accept <name>: the metadata/key failed to process — the sender must resend the file', sends EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT, leaves the entry in WaitingAccept + error, and creates no chunk map (so late-arriving chunks are dropped by the onChunkData guard); without a usable key the transfer can never succeed — an encrypted session would either assemble the raw ciphertext as a Success blob or hit rejectCorruptChunk on every chunk (an N-toast storm per resend) — and only entries that pass the guard emit EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT, flip to Processing, and get their chunk/stats maps.
